long_biography.plain_text:
Returning to Britain in 2009, Malcolm Stanley Healey chose to re-enter the fitted-kitchen trade in his mid-sixties and establish Wren. The decision drew on a career that began in his family's Hull paint and decorating-supplies business, an advantaged commercial starting point. He later built Humber Kitchens, joined MFI in acquiring Hygena, and developed the American cabinet manufacturer Mills Pride before selling his interest in each venture.

At Wren, Healey pursued tighter control of the customer journey by integrating design, manufacturing, delivery and installation. The company expanded from two locations to more than 150 showrooms while retaining extensive factory operations. The model combined volume production and accessible pricing with a national retail network. Healey remains a verified director of Wren Kitchens, The Wren Group, West Retail Group and Wren US Holdings.
